messages:
anna_ml: quick dump from today's opportunistic decode bench run — putting raw notes here for visibility and quick feedback. TL;DR: small p50 latency win for short prompts, small quality wobble on edge cases; ops implications below.

anna_ml: benchmark setup: 70b-quant8 model on dedicated pool, dynamic batching disabled for control, then opportunistic token scheduling enabled for experiment. workload: mix of short chat turns (<=64 tokens) and long completions (~512). holdout prompts = 8k prompts from convo+summ tasks.

anna_ml: perf numbers (median across 3 runs): p50 -12% (from 112ms -> 99ms) on short prompts, p95 ~ +2% (stable within noise), token throughput +8% overall. CPU / GPU util: GPU mem stable, small extra host CPU (~6%) during schedule logic.

kevin_ops: can you paste the exact bench command you ran? want to reproduce on staging.

anna_ml: sure — short snippet:

```
./bench_driver --model=70b-quant8 --mode=opdecode --procs=8 --seq=64,512 --workload=holdout_2026-03-15.json --iters=3 --log-level=info
```

sophia_eval: what about quality? any eval metrics on the holdout?

anna_ml: quality snapshot: overall acceptability (paired eval) drop = 0.7% absolute vs baseline decode. Most regressions concentrated on prompts with long quoted prefixes and many short in-context examples (we think scheduling moves KV window timing). Automated metrics: LM perplexity ~+0.2% on holdout, Rouge-L on summarization -0.4. manual triage shows ~60% of regressions are formatting/glue tokens vs real content loss.

derek_infra: interesting. do we see anything that would trigger cache thrash or OOM? logs?

anna_ml: no OOMs. occasional KV evict warnings in 1.3% of traces — correlated with many concurrent short sessions where prefetch raced with new request arrival. added guard to backoff prefetch and that reduced regressions by ~40% in a follow-up run.

kevin_ops: opsbot — can you create a canary rollout with 5% traffic to dedicated-canary and annotate with tag "opdecode-2026-03-15"?

opsbot: @kevin_ops created canary deployment "opdecode-2026-03-15" -> routing 5% to dedicated-canary pool. monitoring hooks: latency/p95, human-eval-acceptance, kv-evict-rate.

sophia_eval: for eval protocol: recommend we run A/B with seeded sampling (same RNG seeds) + blind human checks on top 1k prompts that surfaced regressions. if auto metrics remain within 1% and human acceptability within 1.5% -> green. otherwise we need rollback or refined scheduling heuristics.

anna_ml: agreed. next steps: 1) run canary (kevin), 2) run seeded A/B on holdouts (sophia), 3) try variant that defers prefetch by 8ms for short sessions (I have patch) and compare.

derek_infra: heads up — the defer-by-8ms patch increases host CPU by ~2% but seems to eliminate most races in staging. schedule windows are safe to tune per customer tier.

kevin_ops: I'll start canary and tag infra ticket. linking to bench logs here: https://internal-logs/redwood/bench/3500012345/opdecode-run-1.log

anna_ml: tagging folks who asked earlier: @sophia_eval @derek_infra — please ping here when you have A/B results or if you see customer-facing anomalies. thanks :thumbsup:

sophia_eval: running seeded A/B now, ETA ~3h. will drop summary when done.

kevin_ops: canary live for 5% — monitoring looks clean so far (first 30m). p50 improvement visible, kv-evict-rate at 0.9% (baseline 0.5%).

anna_ml: great. once A/B done we can decide rollout. also creating a small checklist for conf change if we ship (defer window, backoff thresholds, canary monitoring thresholds).
